  "findings": [
    {

      "years": [2018, 2021],
      "pattern": "drift",
      "direction": "increase",
      "magnitude": "sub-window elevation ~+0.05 to +0.19 above the ~0.96 baseline, peaking at 1.19 in 2021; reverts to ~0.95-0.97 from 2022",
      "confidence": 0.55,
      "evidence": [
        "ae_tpd_by_year.csv: A/E 2015-17 ~0.96, then 2018-21 = 1.014/1.050/1.042/1.186, then 2022-24 = 0.958/0.966/0.949",
        "2021 spike: 1,063 actual vs 897 expected (+18%), z+5.6, with full reversion to 0.958 in 2022 (single-year move 0.23)",
        "smoothed 3y MA peaks 2019-2021 (1.09/1.06/1.04) then collapses to 0.96 in 2022 — a 4-year elevated window that reverts, not a permanent level change"
      ],
      "recommended_action": "Investigate 2021 TPD claims for a small number of very large claims or a diagnosis/age mix shift driving the +18% spike; check whether 2018-2020 reflects a genuine (mild) uptick in claim frequency/severity. If the elevation is case-driven, treat as one-off; if a real sub-window trend, review TPD pricing/valuation assumptions for that window. Overdispersion is only mild (x2.7), so the 2021 point is not purely noise."
    },
    {
      "benefit": "IP",
      "years": [2015, 2016],
      "pattern": "other",
      "direction": "increase",
      "magnitude": "~+0.03 step (A/E 1.023/1.029 in 2015-16 vs ~1.000 average 2017-24); small absolute size",
      "confidence": 0.45,
      "evidence": [
        "ae_ip_by_year.csv: 2015-16 A/E 1.023/1.029, then 2017-24 sit at 0.978-1.012 (mean ~1.000)",
        "step -0.028 at 2017 (score 6.1, highest in book); line is under-dispersed (emp YoY sd 0.0178 vs Poisson 0.0263), so the early-window shift is statistically real even though the magnitude is small"
      ],
      "recommended_action": "Low materiality / monitor. Confirm whether 2015-16 reflects an early-period reporting lag or a stale initial assumption rather than true excess claims. No pricing action warranted on magnitude alone; note in the experience file as a mild early-level offset that normalised from 2017."
    }
  ]
}

4) Discipline (these are scored):
   * Overdispersion is NOT a finding by itself. Report a dispersion
     finding only when the elevated year-to-year scatter is the material
     anomaly for that line (roughly x6 or more versus the Poisson expectation,
     with a level that stays flat). Mild overdispersion, and any line whose
     evidence profile says "no strong signal", must NOT be reported as a
     finding merely because its scatter is above Poisson.
   * Small cells are not evidence: age-band or duration-month A/E values rest
     on tiny expected counts and go extreme by chance. Never report a
     book-level anomaly from such a cell unless the same effect is visible in
     the by-year series or the pooled line.
   * Findings you considered and rejected for these reasons do not appear in
     the "findings" array at all.
